description:
On evals/hashline t6-long-session (7 prompts, gpt-6.1-sol medium, stock thresholds in both), Mastra Code activated OM 8-9 times per session against about 1 for pi-om (Pi with or without hashline). Peak context was about 51k vs 35k. MC also made about 1.7x as many requests and re-read more after edits. Both use the 30k message-token threshold, so the difference must come from what counts toward it (tool-result sizes, message accounting, buffering and activation rules) or from MC's larger tool results.

Do: compare the two on the same task with OM traces (pi-om PI_OM_TRACE; MC om_* events in evals/hashline/harness/mc-run.mjs logs). Account for the message-token totals each side sees per request, and find where they diverge. Do not change thresholds; this is a parity investigation.

Done: a written explanation with per-request evidence of where the activation counts diverge, and either a parity fix in pi-om with a test or a documented, intended difference.
title: OM: why Mastra Code activates OM ~8x more than pi-om on the same session
